name: Expected return and variance with scenarios
formula:
E(R) = Σ p_i R_i
Var(R) = Σ p_i (R_i − E(R))^2
use: Returns given per state of the economy with probabilities.
pitfall: Weights are the probabilities – no T − 1 here.

name: Mean–variance utility
use: Ranking investments for a risk-averse investor.
pitfall: Use the variance, not the volatility.

name: Covariance
formula:
Cov(R_i, R_j) = (1/(T − 1)) Σ (R_{i,t} − R̄_i)(R_{j,t} − R̄_j)
scenarios: Σ p_s (R_{i,s} − E(R_i))(R_{j,s} − E(R_j))
use: How two returns move together (only the sign is easy to read).
pitfall: Historical data: T − 1, like the variance.

name: Correlation
formula: ρ_{i,j} = Cov(R_i, R_j) / (σ_i σ_j)   ⟺   Cov = ρ σ_i σ_j
use: Strength of comovement on a scale from −1 to +1.

name: Beta
formula: β_{j,M} = Cov(R_j, R_M) / Var(R_M) = ρ_{j,M} × σ_j / σ_M
use: How much a stock moves when the market (or another asset) moves by 1%.
pitfall: Divide by the variance of the asset that does the moving.

name: Portfolio return
use: Expected return of any portfolio: a plain weighted average.
vars: x_i = amount in asset i / own money (can be < 0 or > 1)
pitfall: Weights on own money, not on the total position.

name: Portfolio volatility (two assets)
pitfall: Never forget the cross term; a short position flips its sign.

name: Diversification by correlation
use: Quick check of how much diversification a pair offers.
